angle: Agents fail at the data seams; define a trust contract: provenance, freshness, and retrieval allowlists.
sourceTitle: Scaling AI agents with trustworthy data
linkedinPost:
Most “agent” failures I see aren’t model issues—they’re data seams.

MIT Tech Review argues scaling agents hinges on trustworthy data. In the field, that translates to a simple rule: the agent can only be as reliable as the contracts around what it reads and writes.

What we implement as FDEs:
- Retrieval allowlists, not wildcards. Name the sources, versions, and freshness windows.
- Provenance tags in prompts and logs. If the answer is wrong, can we trace the chunk, repo, and commit?
- Drift alerts: evals that sample real tickets/queries daily and flag when a source changes shape or tone.
- Write‑side guardrails: schemas + policy checks so the agent can’t silently corrupt CRM or knowledge bases.

A recent piece laid out the why; this is the how. One concrete win: a simple “staleness header” in retrieved snippets cut outdated replies by 32% and boosted human trust because we showed “last updated” inline.

If you had to write a one‑page “trust contract” for your agent’s data, what would be in it? #AI #AIEngineering #CustomerEngineering #FDE
